newsitem.title: USA: Bond analysts write SEC about muni disclosure woes.
newsitem.headline: Bond analysts write SEC about muni disclosure woes.

text.p: Bond analysts told U.S. regulators on Wednesday that some municipal issuers are violating the spirit, if not the letter, of the SEC's 1994 secondary market disclosure rule.
Rule 15c2-12 bars dealers from underwriting bond offerings unless issuers pledge to provide ongoing disclosure, including notices of material events, to the market through national repositories.

In a letter to the Securities and Exchange Commission, the National Federal of Municipal Analysts (NFMA) said some issuers have stopped sending financial information to analysts directly and are limiting dislosures to only those items mandated in SEC's disclosure rule.

Also, issuers are telling analysts to get the information from national recognized information repositories, which charge fees, NFMA said. And they are refusing to talk to analysts about the data, NFMA said.
They are doing these things on the advice of bond counsel and financial advisers, NFMA said in the two-page letter addressed to SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt.

"The result is that analysts are receiving less information, are paying for it (eventually passing on the cost to investors), and are not able to discuss it with the issuers," said the letter, signed by NFMA Chairman Jeffrey Baker and two other NFMA officials.
And bond counsel are becoming the "determiner of what is provided and how to provide it," NFMA said.

NFMA stressed that uncooperative issuers in the muni market boomare a minority. "However, we are seeing enough instances of an unwillingness to speak to analysts, and to provide data directly, to cause us concern," NFMA said.

The group said hospitals and below investment grade issuers are the biggest culprits, although problems exist in other sectors. "We are concerned that this practice, if it continues unchecked, could become more widespread."

The group said it is not pushing for revisions to Rule 15c2-12, only the SEC's help in encouraging issuers to honor the rule's goals. NFMA officials will discuss the problem with SEC's Office of Municipal Securities at a meeting set for May 20, the group said.
Also signing the letter were Rafael Costas, chairman of the group's industry practices and procedures committee, and Mary Metastasio, chairman of NFMA's disclosure committee.
Baker told Reuters in an interview March 26 that at least 25 issuers are not complying with the rule and that the group is willing to name names if asked.
